## 1. GLOBAL MACRO OVERVIEW

The macro backdrop is decisively stagflationary in character. The US Federal Reserve's April FOMC minutes, released Wednesday, revealed that a majority of officials now see rate hikes as a credible scenario if energy-driven inflation becomes entrenched. The Fed funds rate sits at 3.64% [Source: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/FEDFUNDS], with the effective rate held in the 3.50%–3.75% range since December, but market pricing has shifted dramatically: traders now assign a ~49% probability of a December hike and a 58% chance of a January 2026 hike, per USA Today [Source: https://www.usatoday.com/story/money/economy/2026/05/18/fed-rate-hike-odds-what-it-means/90140362007/]. New Fed Chair Kevin Warsh, a Trump nominee, appears unwilling to cut rates against this inflation backdrop, marking a stark reversal of prior expectations [Source: https://www.forbes.com/sites/tylerroush/2026/05/20/trumps-reshaped-fed-leaning-toward-interest-rate-hikes/].

Inflation data remains hot and sticky. US CPI stands at 3.95% YoY [Source: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/CPIAUCSL] and PPI at 2.66% MoM [Source: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/PPIACO], well above the Fed's 2% target. In the UK, April CPI eased to 2.8% from 3.3%, largely due to Ofgem's energy price cap, but economists warn the relief is temporary as Iran war energy costs continue to feed through [Source: https://www.cnbc.com/amp/2026/05/20/uk-april-inflation-cpi-energy-prices.html]. Canada's April CPI came in at 2.8%, below the 3.1% consensus, as gasoline-driven pressures were partly offset by easing core measures [Source: https://www.kitco.com/news/off-the-wire/2026-05-19/canadian-dollar-hits-five-week-low-cpi-data-clips-rate-hike-bets].

The US Treasury market is the key pressure point. The 10-year yield stands at 4.67% [Source: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DGS10] — near its highest level since February 2025 — with the 30-year reportedly crossing 5.1% intraday on Tuesday, a level not seen since 2007 [Source: https://www.investors.com/market-trend/stock-market-today/dow-jones-sp500-nasdaq-micron-sandisk-home-depot-google-io/]. The 2Y/10Y curve sits at 54 basis points (2Y: 4.13%, 10Y: 4.67%) [Source: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DGS2], reflecting a modest bear steepening as markets price in a prolonged higher-for-longer regime. G7 finance ministers met in Paris to discuss the economic fallout from the Middle East conflict, calling for the immediate reopening of the Strait of Hormuz [Source: https://www.kitco.com/news/off-the-wire/2026-05-19/g7-finance-ministers-agree-need-action-economic-imbalances].

Earnings have offered a mixed backdrop. Target reported Q1 EPS of $1.71, beating adjusted estimates (prior Adj EPS: $1.30), with net sales up 6.7% and comparable store sales +5.6% [Source: https://corporate.target.com/press/release/2026/05/target-corporation-reports-first-quarter-earnings]. Lowe's Q1 adjusted EPS came in at $3.03, up 3.8% YoY, with comparable sales +0.6% [Source: https://markets.ft.com/data/announce/detail?dockey=600-202605200600PR_NEWS_USPRX____CL63495-1]. Nvidia's earnings (Wednesday after-close) remain the market's pivotal event, with Wall Street expecting revenue of $79.12 billion and adjusted EPS of $1.77 [Source: https://www.tipranks.com/news/sp-500-pushes-higher-as-market-braces-for-nvidias-results]. The broader equity rally of 2026 — which pushed Nasdaq and S&P 500 to all-time highs last week — is now facing headwinds from the bond market, even as Barclays notes year-to-date inflows to US equity funds are tracking at $180 billion, more than double the five-year median [Source: https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/market-correction-equities-stocks-bonds-iran-inflation.html].

The Bank of Japan is signalling rate hikes are approaching, with board member Junko Koeda stating Thursday that "it is reasonable for the bank to raise the policy interest rate at an appropriate pace to address high inflation" [Source: https://www.wsj.com/economy/central-banking/bank-of-japan-policymaker-signals-that-rate-hike-might-be-approaching-6a90860b]. This hawkish pivot, combined with a USD/JPY rate at 159.30, is creating mounting pressure on the yen. Bank Indonesia moved first among EM central banks, hiking 50 basis points to 5.25% to stabilise the rupiah [Source: https://www.wsj.com/economy/central-banking/bank-indonesia-delivers-first-rate-hike-in-years-as-rupiah-flounders-risks-rise-af2c5047].

### Disputed

- [Report states "a majority of Fed officials now see rate hikes as a credible scenario"]: Partially inaccurate framing. The Axios article states "a majority" believed the bank *could* raise rates *if inflation stays high* — a conditional scenario, not an active majority preference for hiking. Forbes similarly frames this as Warsh-led board being "less likely to cut" rather than actively favouring hikes. The report's language implies a stronger hawkish consensus than the sources support.

- [Report states USD/JPY at "159.30" in narrative text and dashboard]: Data bundle shows USD/JPY at 159.299 — this is a rounding matter and not materially wrong, but the report selectively rounds to two decimal places inconsistently (e.g., EUR/USD stated as 1.1586 exactly). Not a factual error but worth flagging for precision.

- [Report states the 2Y/10Y spread is "54 basis points" and characterises it as "bear steepening"]: The arithmetic is correct (4.67% - 4.13% = 54bps). However, a bear steepening requires the long end rising faster than the short end. The data bundle does not provide prior-period yield levels to confirm this is steepening vs. parallel shift. The characterisation may be correct contextually (bond selloff focused on long end per news sources), but cannot be fully verified from the bundle alone.

- [Report states BTC "rebound high around $77,070"]: The Business Insider article cites BTC at "$77,070 per Fortune on May 20, rebounding from $76,082." The data bundle shows BTC at $76,759.95 on May 21, which is *below* the cited $77,070 rebound high. The report implies $77,070 as a recent high from which BTC is now pulling back — this is consistent with the data but the $77,070 figure is from a third-party presale news article and should be treated with caution as a precise market reference.

- [Report describes EUR/GBP bias as "Neutral-Bear (EUR)" but then cites Nomura targeting EUR/GBP at "0.8965"]: The Nomura target of 0.8965 is *above* the current 0.8646, implying EUR *strength* against GBP (or GBP weakness), which is inconsistent with the "Neutral-Bear (EUR)" bias label. The source text from exchangerates.org.uk states Nomura's GBP/EUR target is 1.1170, equating to EUR/GBP ~0.8953. If that target is above spot (0.8646), this would be a *EUR-bullish* signal for the cross, contradicting the bias assigned. The report's EUR/GBP bias label appears to be inverted relative to its own cited Nomura forecast.

- [Report cites the 30-year Treasury crossing 5.1% as "a level not seen since 2007"]: Sourced from investors.com, which is in the bundle — confirmed as cited. However, the WSJ livecoverage (May 19) states 10-year yields "hit their highest level since February 2025," not since 2007. The 5.1% figure refers specifically to the 30-year, while the "since 2007" context in the IBD source applies to that threshold crossing. The report correctly attributes this to the 30-year, so this is verified rather than disputed — but traders should note the sources conflate 10Y and 30Y claims in different articles.
